title: Total cost of ownership and hidden on-prem costs

kcs.statement: Total cost of ownership (TCO) counts every cost of running a workload over its life, not just hardware: facilities, power, cooling, networking, software licences and staff time.
On-premises costs that are often left out of comparisons include data center space, power and cooling, physical security, hardware refresh cycles and the people who rack, patch and repair servers.
Moving to the cloud lowers TCO mainly by removing data center overhead and idle capacity, and by freeing staff from undifferentiated heavy lifting to work that serves customers.

problem_ideas: A comparison lists only $200k of server hardware: name four missing on-premises cost lines.
Compute a 3-year TCO: $120k hardware, $30k/yr power and cooling, 1 admin at $90k/yr.
Two admins spend 60% of their time patching hardware: what share of their cost does moving to AWS free up?
Pick which items stay in the TCO after migrating to AWS (licences, staff for the app, building lease).
A manager compares a server's sticker price with an EC2 hourly price: explain why this is not a TCO comparison.
Rank four savings levers by typical impact: idle capacity, power, staff time, hardware refresh.
